1. Calculate the area of the square:
   \[
   \text{Area of the square} = 10 \times 10 = 100 \text{ square centimeters}
   \]

2. Calculate the area of one quarter circle:
   \[
   \text{Area of one quarter circle} = \frac{1}{4} \times \pi \times 10^2 = \frac{1}{4} \times \pi \times 100 = 25\pi \text{ square centimeters}
   \]

3. Calculate the total area of the four quarter circles:
   \[
   \text{Total area of quarter circles} = 4 \times (25\pi) = 100\pi \text{ square centimeters}
   \]

4. Subtract the total area of the quarter circles from the area of the square to find the shaded area:
   \[
   \text{Shaded area} = 100 - 100\pi \text{ square centimeters}
   \]

\[
\boxed{100 - 100\pi}\]

grade.gold_answer: We first notice that the area of the shaded region is the area of the square minus the areas of the four quarter circles. Each quarter circle has a radius half the side length, so if we sum the areas of the four quarter circles, we have the area of one full circle with radius $5$ cm. Now, we know the area of a square is the square of its side length, so the square has an area of $100 \text{ cm}^2$. A circle has an area of $\pi$ times its radius squared, so the four quarter circles combined have an area of $\pi(5)^2=25\pi \text{ cm}^2$. From this, we know that the area of the shaded region is $\boxed{100-25\pi} \text{ cm}^2$.
